newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS - SBC profit growth slows in 3rd qtr.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - SBC profit growth slows in 3rd qtr.

text.p: Swiss Bank Corp (SBC), Switzerland's third biggest bank, said profit growth slowed in the third quarter as world financial markets calmed but it still expected a substantially higher ordinary net profit for 1996.

"From the present perspective, SBC expects that ordinary group profit after taxes for the 1996 financial year will be some percentage points below original estimates, but still substantially higher than in 1995," SBC said in its nine-month statement.
The bank group in September had estimated that 1996 ordinary net profit would rise 33 percent to around 1.4 billion ($1.1) francs.
SBC's nine-month statement said net profit after taxes rose 27 percent in the first nine months of 1996, but provided no figures.
It also reported a 17 percent rise in nine-month net operating income.
Profits had risen by 34 percent to 722 million francs in the 1996 first half.

"At the time we deliberately said we were relatively cautious because it was just hard to believe that the first and second quarter result could just be extrapolated," SBC chief financial officer Peter Wuffli said in a telephone interview.
SBC said the slower third quarter growth was due to lower trading volumes on financial markets, which cut trading income.
Asked for details of the third quarter, Wuffli said a slowdown was seen in equities participation in the U.K. and Switzerland.
Capital market and corporate finance businesses were also slower, but foreign exchange and interest rate activities remained strong on a global basis, he added.
Wuffli said there were now some signs of a pickup in trading volumes at the start of the fourth quarter.
The SBC statement said fourth quarter profit performance would be influenced by financial market trading volumes and by provisioning requirements.

"Overall we do not see any sort of a comback of first second quarter trends, but rather a continuation with a slightly positive uptone from the third quarter," Wuffli said in commenting on the trend in trading.
He also said provisions for the full year would be somewhat higher as compared to the 1.005 billion franc level of 1995.
SBC's provisions for risky loans, after five years of virtual economic stagnation in its Swiss home market, remained at a high level in the third quarter.
"Loan loss provisions were almost exclusively related to exposure in Switzerland, where the economic recovery has been slow to materialise," SBC added.

Union Bank of Switzerland analyst Thomas Kalbermatten said the nine-month results were very positive and in line with his forecast of ordinary net profit after taxes at 1.37 billion francs before extraordinary restructuring costs.

SBC plans to post an extraordinary loss of 1.9 billion this year as its pays for a major restructuring programme announced in September that will slash its ailing domestic bank business, create a new loss reserve for bad loans and change the way it calculates loan risk.
Personnel expenses were lower in the third quarter than in the two previous quarters, mainly due to lower provisions for performance-related compensation. ($1=1.2658 Swiss Franc)
